textual.observation: The tutorial instructs a person to register others through a personal link so signups enter the speaker's downline, and to forward that link to additional people.

evidence.quote: Anyone, who signs up will automatically log off to your downline.
You can then forward this to others.

textual.context: Presented as step-by-step registration guidance; whether the material is promotional or demonstrative is unclear from these records.
textual.potential_relevance: The registration action is explicitly tied to downline placement and onward recruitment, creating a recruitment-related structure that may require later assessment of how participation and any associated benefits are represented.
textual.limitations: No reward, return, fee amount, participant outcome, or completed signup is established by these records.

textual.observation: The tutorial directs the registrant to enter multiple personal and account fields, including a phone number and security code, then select a package and proceed through banking or bank-transfer steps.

evidence.quote: Then you fill in everything you need. The username, email, password, Name, Nickname, the country, the phone number and then the Security code.
then you'll be asked which package you are going to buy.
Then you go to banking transaction and click on ok.

textual.context: The source describes an instructional account-registration and package-purchase flow.
textual.potential_relevance: The source links entry of personal, contact, and security information to a package purchase and bank-transfer step, so later review may need to assess what data and payment are requested and under what stated conditions.
textual.limitations: No recipient identity, transaction completion, security-code purpose, fee amount, or outcome is established; the ASR may contain transcription errors.

visual.observation: A payment page shows an "Executive Trader" package priced at 3000 EUR with a bank-wire option, followed by a popup instructing the viewer to send a bank transfer to listed company and bank details. Separate package displays list euro-priced tiers with free tokens and recurring points.
visual.context: Visible commercial package-purchase flow; no explicit warning or independent qualification is visible in these frames.
visual.potential_relevance: A notable payment request is visibly paired with advertised token and points benefits, creating a payment-for-return relationship that conditionally merits review.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish whether any transfer occurred, whether the listed recipient is legitimate, or whether the advertised benefits were delivered.

visual.observation: The registration interface requests account credentials and personal details, including an email address, password, name, country, mobile phone, and security code, while the same site presents token, bonus, and points account features.
visual.context: Account-registration context is visible, but the sampled frames do not state whether submitting the information is required to access the displayed benefits.
visual.potential_relevance: A sensitive-data signup flow is visibly paired with advertised token, bonus, and points features, which conditionally merits review as a data-request-for-benefit relationship.
visual.limitations: The frames do not show how the submitted information is used, whether registration was completed, or whether the displayed balances are real or redeemable.

visual.observation: The profile page displays an invite link, a control to show a new member with the link owner as sponsor, and left/right placement options; the dashboard also shows a directly sponsored count and a credits balance.
visual.context: A visible referral or sponsorship workflow is present, but the frames do not explain how credits are calculated or whether they depend on recruiting new members.
visual.potential_relevance: Recruitment and member-placement controls are visibly paired with sponsor tracking and credits, conditionally meriting review as a possible referral-reward relationship.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not establish that recruitment was requested from viewers, that credits result from recruitment, or that any payment or benefit was received.

textual_context_notes.observation: The description frames the material as a how-to demonstration for registering someone with OneCoin.

evidence.quote: Here I show you how to register someone with OneCoin.

visual_context_notes.observation: The dashboard visibly tracks token, cash, trading, bonus, points, sponsorship, and credits balances, with a countdown labeled for the next bonus round.
A package-comparison screen visibly presents multiple euro-priced tiers alongside listed token and points quantities.
The profile page visibly labels an invite link and provides sponsor-placement settings for new members.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes enrolling people into a paid package-based network and explicitly places new signups into the recruiter's downline. It instructs viewers to use an invite link, choose a package, and complete a bank transfer while the accompanying dashboard displays bonuses, points, sponsored members, and leadership rank. The central action is encouraging participation in a recruitment-dependent earning structure, not neutrally explaining an ordinary registration process.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S06 applies because the video presents a multi-person downline/upline structure, placement of recruits on the left or right side, and bonus or qualification indicators connected to recruited members. The participation flow requires selecting and paying for a package and then recruiting others through an invite link.
